Advanced · lesson 7

Layout follows access

src/7.access_patterns/access_patterns.rin

src/7.access_patterns/access_patterns.rin

Lesson 1 found the layout SIMD wants: one array per float. This lesson asks what that layout costs everywhere else. 1,048,576 bodies are stored four ways, and two kinds of loop run over each, and the program checks that all four end with the same positions.

Two kinds of loop

Stream: every body, in order, the same math. Integration is the example:

for (i: u64 = 0; i < px.length; i += 1) {
    px[i] += vx[i] * dt;
    ...
}

The next body is always right after the last one, so the hardware prefetcher has it ready, and SIMD can take four or eight at once if they sit side by side.

Lookup: bodies picked by index, two at a time, in no particular order. Contacts are the example, the way collision and constraints reach bodies:

a: u64 = cast(cs[c].a, u64);
b: u64 = cast(cs[c].b, u64);
dx: f32 = px[b] - px[a];
...

Each body is somewhere else in memory. What matters is how many cache lines one body's data sits in, because each one is a separate trip to memory. SIMD does not help: there are no four neighbours to load at once.

Four layouts

aos      [ x y z vx vy vz m r ][ x y z vx vy vz m r ] ...      32 bytes a body
columns  positions  [ x y z ][ x y z ][ x y z ] ...
         velocities [ vx vy vz ][ vx vy vz ] ...                 24 bytes a body
split    px [ x x x x ... ]   py [ y y y y ... ]   pz ...  vx ...  vy ...  vz ...
blocks   [ x0..x7 | y0..y7 | z0..z7 | vx0..vx7 | vy0..vy7 | vz0..vz7 ][ x8..x15 ...
  • aos keeps everything about a body together, two fields neither loop uses included.
  • columns is one array per component, each component a small struct. This is what an ECS table stores, and what lessons 2 to 6 use.
  • split is one array per float, lesson 1's move_split.
  • blocks is eight bodies at a time, each coordinate a run of eight floats. It is split cut into pieces of eight, with the pieces of one body kept near each other. The usual name is AoSoA, an array of structs of arrays.

The program prints how many 64-byte cache lines one body's position sits in:

cache lines one lookup touches: aos 1.000, columns 1.125, split 3.000, blocks 2.000

A 12-byte vec3 crosses a line boundary 2 times in 16, hence 1.125. In split, x, y and z are in three different arrays. In a block, x and y share a line and z is in the next.

Measured

Release, clang -O2, best of three runs, on the 2.8 GHz Xeon these lessons were checked on: 4 MB of L2, 33 MB of L3. The body count was changed in the generated C for the first and last columns. At 65,536 bodies each layout fits in L2; at the lesson's 1,048,576 each is about the size of L3; at 8,388,608 each is 192 to 256 MB and comes from RAM.

Stream, ns per body:

layout65,5361,048,5768,388,608
aos1.674.204.09
columns1.682.082.88
split0.931.301.66
blocks0.701.622.79

Lookup, ns per contact:

layout65,5361,048,5768,388,608
aos5.0326.2750.35
columns3.4211.9440.35
split6.5428.2295.01
blocks5.9825.7061.20

clang with -mavx2 -mfma and gcc -O3 agree on the main points: split streams fastest from RAM, columns look up fastest at every size, and split looks up slowest from RAM. Where two numbers are within about 20 percent, the order changes from build to build; gcc -O3, for one, streamed columns fastest at a million bodies. The machine is shared; expect about 20 percent noise.

What it says:

  • Split wins the stream and loses the lookup. From RAM it streams 1.7 times faster than columns, and looks up 2.4 times slower: three lines a body instead of one.
  • Columns win the lookup everywhere and come second or third in the stream. AoS also has one line a body, but its bodies are 32 bytes, so the same lookups spread over more memory. At a million bodies, columns' positions are 12 MB and sit comfortably in L3; AoS spreads them over 32 MB, about all of it.
  • Blocks are the compromise. In L2 they streamed fastest of all, and a little behind split at a million bodies. They look up better than split at every size. From RAM their stream fell back to about columns' speed on this machine, which I have not explained.
  • Out of cache, a lookup costs ten to fifty times a streamed body. From RAM, 40 to 95 ns a contact against 2 to 4 ns a body. Turning lookups into something closer to a stream, by sorting contacts or walking space in order, usually saves more than any layout choice.

integrate_blocks, /arch:AVX28140
contacts_columns1 contact250
contacts_split1 contact320

Blocks vectorize as cleanly as split: the inner loop over eight lanes is a fixed-size loop over consecutive floats, which compilers turn into whole registers. The contact loops are one contact a pass in every layout.

In between

Engines that have both kinds of loop do one of these:

  • Blocks, as above. One layout, decent at both.
  • Gather, work, scatter. Storage stays in columns or AoS, good for lookups. The hot loop copies a batch of bodies into a wide layout, x's in one register and y's in another, does its math, and copies them back. The copy pays off when the same batch is worked on many times, as a constraint solver does over several iterations. Box2D v3 solves contacts this way, four or eight at a time.
  • Two layouts for two jobs. A particle system that only ever streams stores split. The bodies that collision looks up stay in columns.

How an ECS decides

An ECS does not decide where each float goes. The component is the unit it stores together, and the programmer decides what a component is.

  • Tables. kayan, Unity's entities, Bevy and flecs keep one table per archetype, with one column per component. That is this lesson's columns layout: an array per component, and each component's fields side by side inside it. Unity cuts its tables into 16 KB chunks, each holding every component array for as many entities as fit, which is close to blocks at the level of components.
  • Sparse sets. EnTT stores each component in its own dense array with a lookup table from entity to index, and can keep several components in the same order ("groups") so a system over them streams. Bevy lets each component choose: table storage, or a sparse set for components added and removed often.
  • Systems are streams. A system is a query and a kernel, as in lesson 6: the ECS finds the tables that match, and hands the kernel each table's columns. That stream over columns is the fast path every ECS is built for. Systems that say which columns they read and which they write are what lets a scheduler run them in parallel.
  • Lookups go through the handle. Reaching one entity is handle, slot, table and row, then the column: kayan_get in lesson 4. That is this lesson's lookup loop with an extra hop in front. ECS code keeps lookups for the places that need them, such as relationships between entities and collision, and finds the rest by query.

So the decisions that are yours:

  1. Keep components small, to what one stream system reads. A component a system reads half of is AoS's wasted bytes again.
  2. Leave components as small structs, position { x, y, z }, unless a profiler shows a stream over them is the bottleneck. They are the best layout for lookups and good enough for most streams.
  3. For a hot stream over huge counts, particles above all, store split or blocks, or gather into them for the hot loop.
  4. Make lookups rarer and less random before tuning their layout.

Try

  1. Sort cs by a before the timing loops and run --time again. Which lookup numbers change, and by how much?
  2. Set body_count and contact_count to 8388608 and run --time in Release. Compare with the tables above.
  3. Make the contacts push velocities too, vx, vy and vz of both bodies. How many lines does a lookup touch in each layout now?
  4. Add /arch:AVX2 to build_c_flags and compare the stream column.
  5. Write contacts_gather: for every eight contacts, copy the sixteen bodies' positions into [8]f32 arrays, do the arithmetic over the arrays, and copy back. Contacts that share a body in the same eight break it; find the case and decide what to do about it.
  6. Make body 64 bytes with fields neither loop uses, and watch aos in both tables.

The old columns stay in the arena unused: an126// arena does not free single allocations, and these lessons accept the waste.127kayan_table_grow: proc(w: *kayan_world, t: *kayan_table) -> void = {128    capacity: u64 = t*.capacity == 0 ? 16 : t*.capacity * 2;129    entities: ^kayan_entity = cast(memops_arena_push_zero(w*.arena,130        sizeof(kayan_entity) * capacity, alignof(kayan_entity)), ^kayan_entity);131    if (t*.count > 0) {132        memcpy(entities, t*.entities, sizeof(kayan_entity) * t*.count);133    }134    t*.entities = entities;135    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w*.component_count; id += 1) {136        if ((t*.signature & kayan_bit(id)) != 0) {137            info: *const reflect = w*.infos[id];138            column: ^u8 = cast(memops_arena_push_zero(w*.arena, info*.size * capacity,139                info*.align), ^u8);140            if (t*.count > 0) {141                memcpy(column, t*.columns[id], info*.size * t*.count);142            }143            t*.columns[id] = column;144        }145    }146    t*.capacity = capacity;147}148 149// The table for a signature, made the first time anything needs it.150kayan_table_for: proc(w: *kayan_world, signature: u64) -> u32 = {151    found: *u32 = hashmap<u64, u32>get(w*.by_signature&, signature);152    if (found != null) {153        return found*;154    }155    for (id: u32 = 0; id < 64; id += 1) {156        if ((signature & kayan_bit(id)) != 0 && (id >= w*.component_count || w*.infos[id] == null)) {157            printfmt("kayan: signature {} uses component {}, which was never registered\n", signature, id);158            exit(1);159        }160    }161    t: kayan_table = {};162    t.signature = signature;163    index: u32 = cast(w*.tables.length, u32);164    vec<kayan_table>append(w*.arena, w*.tables&, t);165    hashmap<u64, u32>put(w*.arena, w*.by_signature&, signature, index);166    return index;167}168 169// A new row with zeroed components, owned by `e`.170kayan_table_add_row: proc(w: *kayan_world, t: *kayan_table, e: kayan_entity) -> u64 = {171    if (t*.count == t*.capacity) {172        kayan_table_grow(w, t);173    }174    row: u64 = t*.count;175    t*.entities[row] = e;176    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w*.component_count; id += 1) {177        if (t*.columns[id] != null) {178            size: u64 = w*.infos[id]*.size;179            memset(t*.columns[id][row * size]&, 0, size);180        }181    }182    t*.count += 1;183    return row;184}185 186// Swap-remove: the last row moves into `row`, and the slot of the entity that187// moved is told its new row. This is the line lesson 2 could not write.188kayan_table_remove_row: proc(w: *kayan_world, t: *kayan_table, row: u64) -> void = {189    last: u64 = t*.count - 1;190    if (row != last) {191        for (id: u32 = 0; id < w*.component_count; id += 1) {192            if (t*.columns[id] != null) {193                size: u64 = w*.infos[id]*.size;194                memcpy(t*.columns[id][row * size]&, t*.columns[id][last * size]&, size);195            }196        }197        moved: kayan_entity = t*.entities[last];198        t*.entities[row] = moved;199        vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots&, cast(moved.index, u64))*.row = cast(row, u32);200    }201    t*.count = last;202}203 204kayan_matches: proc(t: *kayan_table, q: kayan_query) -> b32 = {205    return (t*.signature & q.all) == q.all && (t*.signature & q.none) == 0;206}207 208// T's column, cut to the rows in use. Asking for a column the table does not209// have is a bug in the caller, so it stops the program.210kayan_column: proc<T>(t: *kayan_table) -> []T = {211    id: u32 = kayan_id_of<T>();212    if (t*.columns[id] == null) {213        printfmt("kayan: table {} has no column for component {}\n", t*.signature, id);214        exit(1);215    }216    raw: ^T = cast(t*.columns[id], ^T);217    return raw[0..t*.count];218}219 220kayan_table_entities: proc(t: *kayan_table) -> []kayan_entity = {221    return t*.entities[0..t*.count];222}223 224// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------225// Entities226// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------227 228kayan_alive: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> b32 = {229    if (cast(e.index, u64) >= w*.slots.length) {230        return 0;231    }232    return vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots&, cast(e.index, u64))*.generation == e.generation;233}234 235// A new entity with the components in `signature`, all zeroed. A freed index is236// reused before a new one is made, with the generation its despawn left behind.237kayan_spawn: proc(w: *kayan_world, signature: u64) -> kayan_entity = {238    e: kayan_entity = {};239    if (!vec<u32>is_empty(w*.free&)) {240        e.index = vec<u32>pop(w*.free&);241    } else {242        e.index = cast(w*.slots.length, u32);243        vec<kayan_slot>append(w*.arena, w*.slots&, { .generation = 1 });244    }245    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots&, cast(e.index, u64));246    e.generation = slot*.generation;247 248    table_index: u32 = kayan_table_for(w, signature);249    t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, table_index);250    row: u64 = kayan_table_add_row(w, t, e);251 252    slot*.table = table_index;253    slot*.row = cast(row, u32);254    w*.live += 1;255    return e;256}257 258// A dead handle reports `dead`, so despawning twice is harmless.259kayan_despawn: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> kayan_status = {260    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {261        return kayan_status.dead;262    }263    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots&, cast(e.index, u64));264    kayan_table_remove_row(w, kayan_table_at(w, slot*.table), cast(slot*.row, u64));265    slot*.generation += 1;266    vec<u32>append(w*.arena, w*.free&, e.index);267    w*.live -= 1;268    return kayan_status.ok;269}270 271kayan_signature: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> u64 = {272    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {273        return 0;274    }275    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots&, cast(e.index, u64));276    return kayan_table_at(w, slot*.table)*.signature;277}278 279// Move `e` to the table for `signature`. Components both tables have are280// copied; components only the new table has start zeroed; components only the281// old table has are dropped.282kayan_move: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, signature: u64) -> kayan_status = {283    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {284        return kayan_status.dead;285    }286    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots&, cast(e.index, u64));287    from_index: u32 = slot*.table;288    if (kayan_table_at(w, from_index)*.signature == signature) {289        return kayan_status.ok;290    }291    // kayan_table_for may add a table, so the table pointers are taken after it.292    to_index: u32 = kayan_table_for(w, signature);293    from: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, from_index);294    to: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, to_index);295    from_row: u64 = cast(slot*.row, u64);296    to_row: u64 = kayan_table_add_row(w, to, e);297    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w*.component_count; id += 1) {298        if (from*.columns[id] != null && to*.columns[id] != null) {299            size: u64 = w*.infos[id]*.size;300            memcpy(to*.columns[id][to_row * size]&, from*.columns[id][from_row * size]&, size);301        }302    }303    kayan_table_remove_row(w, from, from_row);304    slot*.table = to_index;305    slot*.row = cast(to_row, u32);306    return kayan_status.ok;307}308 309// e's T, or null if e is dead or has no T. The row is checked against the310// rows in use, so a slot pointing past the end stops the program in Debug.311kayan_get: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> *T = {312    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {313        return null;314    }315    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots&, cast(e.index, u64));316    t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, slot*.table);317    if (t*.columns[kayan_id_of<T>()] == null) {318        return null;319    }320    rows: []T = kayan_column<T>(t);321    return rows[cast(slot*.row, u64)]&;322}323 324// e's component `id` as its bytes, or an empty slice if e is dead or has no325// such component. For tools that work from reflection records rather than from326// types, like lesson 5's inspector.327kayan_get_bytes: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, id: u32) -> []u8 = {328    none: []u8 = {};329    if (!kayan_alive(w, e) || id >= w*.component_count) {330        return none;331    }332    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots&, cast(e.index, u64));333    t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, slot*.table);334    if (t*.columns[id] == null) {335        return none;336    }337    size: u64 = w*.infos[id]*.size;338    column: []u8 = t*.columns[id][0..t*.count * size];339    row: u64 = cast(slot*.row, u64);340    return column[row * size..(row + 1) * size];341}342 343// Give e a T, moving it to a new table if it did not have one.344kayan_add: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, value: T) -> kayan_status = {345    if (kayan_move(w, e, kayan_signature(w, e) | kayan_mask_of<T>()) == kayan_status.dead) {346        return kayan_status.dead;347    }348    kayan_get<T>(w, e)* = value;349    return kayan_status.ok;350}351 352// Take e's T away, moving it to the table without it.353kayan_remove: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> kayan_status = {354    return kayan_move(w, e, kayan_signature(w, e) & ~kayan_mask_of<T>());355}356 357// Every row of every table must belong to a live entity whose slot points back358// at that table and row, and the rows must add up to the live count. Returns359// how many of those checks failed, printing each.360kayan_verify: proc(w: *kayan_world) -> u64 = {361    problems: u64 = 0;362    rows: u64 = 0;363    for (ti: u64 = 0; ti < w*.tables.length; ti += 1) {364        t: *kayan_table = vec<kayan_table>at(w*.tables&, ti);365        ids: []kayan_entity = kayan_table_entities(t);366        for (row: u64 = 0; row < ids.length; row += 1) {367            e: kayan_entity = ids[row];368            if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {369                printfmt("kayan_verify: table {} row {} holds dead entity {}:{}\n",370                    ti, row, e.index, e.generation);371                problems += 1;372                continue;373            }374            slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w*.slots&, cast(e.index, u64));375            if (cast(slot*.table, u64) != ti || cast(slot*.row, u64) != row) {376                printfmt("kayan_verify: {}:{} is in table {} row {}, its slot says table {} row {}\n",377                    e.index, e.generation, ti, row, slot*.table, slot*.row);378                problems += 1;379            }380        }381        rows += t*.count;382    }383    if (rows != w*.live) {384        printfmt("kayan_verify: {} rows in tables, {} entities alive\n", rows, w*.live);385        problems += 1;386    }387    return problems;388}389 390// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------391// Printing392// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------393 394kayan_print_signature: proc(w: *kayan_world, signature: u64) -> void = {395    printf("{");396    first: b32 = 1;397    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w*.component_count; id += 1) {398        if ((signature & kayan_bit(id)) != 0) {399            printf(first ? "%s" : " %s", kayan_component_name(w, id));400            first = 0;401        }402    }403    printf("}");404}405 406kayan_print_tables: proc(w: *kayan_world) -> void = {407    for (ti: u64 = 0; ti < w*.tables.length; ti += 1) {408        t: *kayan_table = vec<kayan_table>at(w*.tables&, ti);409        printf("    table %d ", cast(ti, i32));410        kayan_print_signature(w, t*.signature);411        printf(":");412        for (row: u64 = 0; row < t*.count; row += 1) {413            printf(" %u:%u", t*.entities[row].index, t*.entities[row].generation);414        }415        printf("\n");416    }417}

Tooling

Build and check

tools/check.py runs every program and diffs its output

tools/check.py

1"""Build every lesson, run it, and compare what it prints with its .expected file.2 3    python tools/check.py               every lesson4    python tools/check.py archetype     only lessons whose path contains "archetype"5    python tools/check.py --bless       rewrite the .expected files from this run6    python tools/check.py --sanitize    also build with AddressSanitizer and UBSan7 8A lesson passes only if all four steps are clean:9 10  1. `rin compile` prints nothing but its "generated" line,11  2. the C compiler reports no warnings (-Wall -Wextra -Werror),12  3. the program exits with 0,13  4. its output matches the .expected file beside it, byte for byte.14 15The lessons are the list in build.rin, so there is one list to keep. The16dojo's playgrounds are in it too. Each dojo block is also checked on its own17(`python tools/check.py dojo` for only them): its solution.rin, a whole program18that imports the harness, must build and print its harness.expected;19level1.rin must build and fail, since it has a gap; level2.rin must build.20 21rin is found through RIN, then RIN_HOME, then PATH; its std is the folder beside22it, as `rin build` assumes. The C compiler is CC, or clang.23"""24 25from __future__ import annotations26 27import os28import re29import shutil30import subprocess31import sys32from pathlib import Path33 34ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent35OUT = ROOT / "build" / "check"36 37 38def find_rin() -> Path:39    names = ["rin.exe", "rin"] if os.name == "nt" else ["rin", "rin.exe"]40    if os.environ.get("RIN"):41        return Path(os.environ["RIN"])42    if os.environ.get("RIN_HOME"):43        for name in names:44            candidate = Path(os.environ["RIN_HOME"]) / name45            if candidate.exists():46                return candidate47    for name in names:48        found = shutil.which(name)49        if found:50            return Path(found)51    sys.exit("check: rin not found; set RIN or RIN_HOME, or put rin on PATH")52 53 54def list_from_build_rin(name: str) -> list[str] | None:55    text = (ROOT / "build.rin").read_text(encoding="utf-8")56    block = re.search(rf"^{name}:[^{{]*\{{(.*?)\}}", text, re.S | re.M)57    if not block:58        return None59    return re.findall(r'"([^"]+)"', block.group(1))60 61 62def lessons_from_build_rin() -> list[Path]:63    entries = list_from_build_rin("build_entries")64    if entries is None:65        sys.exit("check: no build_entries in build.rin")66    return [ROOT / entry for entry in entries]67 68 69def run(cmd: list[str], cwd: Path = ROOT,70        env: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:71    return subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=cwd, env=env, text=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,72                          stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=300)73 74 75# On Windows a sanitized program loads clang_rt.asan_dynamic-x86_64.dll when it76# starts, and exits with 0xC0000135 before main if the DLL is not on PATH. It77# lives in the C compiler's own resource directory, so ask the compiler.78def sanitizer_env(cc: str) -> dict[str, str] | None:79    if os.name != "nt":80        return None81    resource = run([cc, "-print-resource-dir"]).stdout.strip()82    runtime = Path(resource) / "lib" / "windows"83    if not runtime.is_dir():84        return None85    env = dict(os.environ)86    env["PATH"] = str(runtime) + os.pathsep + env.get("PATH", "")87    return env88 89 90def check(rin: Path, cc: str, lesson: Path, bless: bool, sanitize: bool,91          env: dict[str, str] | None) -> tuple[bool, str]:92    stem = lesson.stem93    work = OUT / stem94    work.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)95    c_path = work / f"{stem}.c"96    exe = work / (f"{stem}.exe" if os.name == "nt" else stem)97 98    translate = run([str(rin), "compile", str(lesson), "-o", str(c_path),99                     "--header", str(work / f"{stem}.h")])100    noise = [line for line in translate.stdout.splitlines()101             if line.strip() and not line.startswith("rin: generated")]102    if translate.returncode != 0 or noise:103        return False, "rin compile:\n" + translate.stdout104 105    flags = ["-std=c11", "-g", "-Wall", "-Wextra", "-Werror"]106    flags += [f"-D{define}" for define in list_from_build_rin("build_defines") or []]107    if sanitize:108        flags += ["-fsanitize=address,undefined", "-fno-sanitize-recover=all"]109    includes = ["-I", str(rin.parent), "-I", str(rin.parent / "std")]110    libs = [] if os.name == "nt" else ["-lm"]111    build = run([cc, *flags, *includes, str(c_path), "-o", str(exe), *libs])112    if build.returncode != 0 or build.stdout.strip():113        return False, f"{cc}:\n" + build.stdout114 115    ran = run([str(exe)], env=env)116    if ran.returncode != 0:117        return False, f"exit {ran.returncode}:\n{ran.stdout}"118 119    actual = ran.stdout.replace("\r\n", "\n")120    expected_path = lesson.with_suffix(".expected")121    if bless:122        expected_path.write_text(actual, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")123        return True, "blessed"124    if not expected_path.exists():125        return False, f"no {expected_path.name}; run with --bless after reading the output:\n{actual}"126    expected = expected_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("\r\n", "\n")127    if actual != expected:128        got, want = actual.splitlines(), expected.splitlines()129        for i in range(max(len(got), len(want))):130            g = got[i] if i < len(got) else "<missing>"131            w = want[i] if i < len(want) else "<missing>"132            if g != w:133                return False, f"line {i + 1}\n  got:  {g}\n  want: {w}"134    return True, ""135 136 137# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the dojo138 139DOJO = ROOT / "dojo"140# A kata in progress is full of unused parameters and locals.141KATA_QUIET = ["-Wno-unused-parameter", "-Wno-unused-variable", "-Wno-unused-but-set-variable",142              "-Wno-unused-function"]143 144 145def dojo_blocks() -> list[Path]:146    return sorted((p for p in DOJO.iterdir() if p.is_dir() and re.match(r"\d+\.", p.name)),147                  key=lambda p: int(p.name.split(".")[0]))148 149 150# A kata file is a whole program: it imports what it uses and the harness,151# which has main, so each of the solution and the levels builds where it is.152def dojo_build(rin: Path, cc: str, block: Path, kata: Path, where: str, sanitize: bool,153               quiet: bool) -> tuple[Path | None, str]:154    folder = OUT / "dojo" / block.name155    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)156    c_path = folder / f"{where}.c"157    exe = folder / (f"{where}.exe" if os.name == "nt" else where)158    translate = run([str(rin), "compile", str(kata), "-o", str(c_path),159                     "--header", str(folder / f"{where}.h")])160    noise = [line for line in translate.stdout.splitlines()161             if line.strip() and not line.startswith("rin: generated")]162    if translate.returncode != 0 or noise:163        return None, "rin compile:\n" + translate.stdout164    flags = ["-std=c11", "-g", "-Wall", "-Wextra", "-Werror", *(KATA_QUIET if quiet else [])]165    flags += [f"-D{define}" for define in list_from_build_rin("build_defines") or []]166    if sanitize:167        flags += ["-fsanitize=address,undefined", "-fno-sanitize-recover=all"]168    includes = ["-I", str(rin.parent), "-I", str(rin.parent / "std")]169    libs = [] if os.name == "nt" else ["-lm"]170    build = run([cc, *flags, *includes, str(c_path), "-o", str(exe), *libs])171    if build.returncode != 0 or build.stdout.strip():172        return None, f"{cc}:\n" + build.stdout173    return exe, ""174 175 176def check_dojo(rin: Path, cc: str, block: Path, bless: bool, sanitize: bool,177               env: dict[str, str] | None) -> tuple[bool, str]:178    exe, err = dojo_build(rin, cc, block, block / "solution.rin", "solution", sanitize, False)179    if not exe:180        return False, "solution.rin, " + err181    ran = run([str(exe)], env=env)182    if ran.returncode != 0:183        return False, f"the solution fails its harness, exit {ran.returncode}:\n{ran.stdout}"184    actual = ran.stdout.replace("\r\n", "\n")185    expected_path = block / "harness.expected"186    detail = ""187    if bless:188        expected_path.write_text(actual, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")189        detail = "blessed"190    elif not expected_path.exists():191        return False, f"no harness.expected; run with --bless after reading the output:\n{actual}"192    elif actual != expected_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("\r\n", "\n"):193        return False, "the harness's output with the solution is not harness.expected"194    for level in (1, 2):195        exe, err = dojo_build(rin, cc, block, block / f"level{level}.rin", f"level{level}", sanitize, True)196        if not exe:197            return False, f"level{level}.rin, " + err198        if level == 1 and run([str(exe)], env=env).returncode == 0:199            return False, "level 1 passes the harness as given; its gap is not a gap"200    return True, detail201 202 203def main() -> int:204    args = sys.argv[1:]205    bless = "--bless" in args206    sanitize = "--sanitize" in args207    filters = [a for a in args if not a.startswith("--")]208 209    rin = find_rin()210    cc = os.environ.get("CC", "clang")211    lessons = [l for l in lessons_from_build_rin()212               if not filters or any(f in str(l) for f in filters)]213 214    env = sanitizer_env(cc) if sanitize else None215 216    failed = 0217    for lesson in lessons:218        ok, detail = check(rin, cc, lesson, bless, sanitize, env)219        name = lesson.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()220        print(f"{'ok  ' if ok else 'FAIL'} {name}" + (f"  ({detail})" if ok and detail else ""))221        if not ok:222            failed += 1223            print("     " + detail.replace("\n", "\n     "))224    print(f"{len(lessons) - failed} of {len(lessons)} passed")225 226    blocks = [b for b in dojo_blocks()227              if not filters or any(f in b.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix() for f in filters)]228    dojo_failed = 0229    for block in blocks:230        ok, detail = check_dojo(rin, cc, block, bless, sanitize, env)231        print(f"{'ok  ' if ok else 'FAIL'} {block.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()}, the solution and the levels"232              + (f"  ({detail})" if ok and detail else ""))233        if not ok:234            dojo_failed += 1235            print("     " + detail.replace("\n", "\n     "))236    if blocks:237        print(f"{len(blocks) - dojo_failed} of {len(blocks)} dojo blocks passed")238    return 1 if failed or dojo_failed else 0239 240 241if __name__ == "__main__":242    sys.exit(main())

1"""The dojo's runner: start a kata, run it against its harness, keep your times.2 3    python tools/dojo.py                         the blocks, your reps, and what is due4    python tools/dojo.py start slot_map 2        a fresh kata.rin from level 2; the clock starts5    python tools/dojo.py slot_map                build the harness with your kata.rin and run it6    python tools/dojo.py slot_map --seed 42 --stop 13377                                                 the same fuzz run, stopping before operation 13378    python tools/dojo.py slot_map --sanitize     with AddressSanitizer and UBSan9    python tools/dojo.py play slot_map           the block's playground10 11A block can be named by its number, its name, or the start of its name:12`3`, `slot_map` and `slot` are the same block.13 14When a started kata passes, the time since `start` is added to dojo/log.md,15and the block is due again after 1, 3, 7, 14, then 30 days, counting its16passes. Spaced reps are what make a block stick, more than many in one day.17 18If the harness crashes rather than failing a check (an out-of-bounds index,19say), the runner runs it again with --trace to show the operation that was20running.21 22Your kata.rin files are yours: git ignores them, and `start` will not23overwrite one you have changed unless you add --force. A kata is a whole24program: it imports what it uses and the harness, which has main, so the25runner builds kata.rin, and the harness comes with it. rin and the C compiler26are found as tools/check.py finds them.27"""28 29from __future__ import annotations30 31import datetime as dt32import json33import os34import re35import shutil36import subprocess37import sys38from pathlib import Path39 40sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))41from check import find_rin, list_from_build_rin  # noqa: E40242 43ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent44DOJO = ROOT / "dojo"45OUT = ROOT / "build" / "dojo"46LOG = DOJO / "log.md"47STARTED = DOJO / ".started.json"48INTERVALS = [1, 3, 7, 14, 30]49 50 51def blocks() -> list[Path]:52    return sorted((p for p in DOJO.iterdir() if p.is_dir() and re.match(r"\d+\.", p.name)),53                  key=lambda p: int(p.name.split(".")[0]))54 55 56def name_of(block: Path) -> str:57    return block.name.split(".", 1)[1]58 59 60def find(word: str) -> Path:61    found = [b for b in blocks() if word in (b.name, name_of(b), b.name.split(".")[0])]62    found = found or [b for b in blocks() if name_of(b).startswith(word)]63    if len(found) != 1:64        sys.exit(f"dojo: no single block called {word!r}; the blocks are "65                 + ", ".join(name_of(b) for b in blocks()))66    return found[0]67 68 69# The target times, from the level table in each block's README:70# | 2 | every proc | 8:00 |71def targets(block: Path) -> dict[int, str]:72    readme = block / "README.md"73    text = readme.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if readme.exists() else ""74    return {int(m.group(1)): m.group(2) for m in re.finditer(r"^\| (\d) \|.*\| (\d+:\d\d) \|$", text, re.M)}75 76 77# rin writes C, and the C compiler does the rest, as tools/check.py does. A78# kata in progress is full of unused parameters and locals, so the warnings for79# those are off and warnings are not errors; tools/check.py builds the80# solutions with -Werror and every warning on.81def build(source: Path, exe: Path, sanitize: bool) -> None:82    exe.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)83    rin = find_rin()84    c_path = exe.with_suffix(".c")85    translate = subprocess.run([str(rin), "compile", str(source), "-o", str(c_path),86                                "--header", str(exe.with_suffix(".h"))], text=True,87                               stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)88    noise = [l for l in translate.stdout.splitlines() if l.strip() and not l.startswith("rin: generated")]89    if translate.returncode != 0 or noise:90        print(translate.stdout, end="")91        sys.exit(1)92    cc = os.environ.get("CC", "clang")93    flags = ["-std=c11", "-g", "-Wall", "-Wextra", "-Wno-unused-parameter", "-Wno-unused-variable",94             "-Wno-unused-but-set-variable", "-Wno-unused-function"]95    flags += [f"-D{define}" for define in list_from_build_rin("build_defines") or []]96    if sanitize:97        flags += ["-fsanitize=address,undefined", "-fno-sanitize-recover=all"]98    includes = ["-I", str(rin.parent), "-I", str(rin.parent / "std")]99    libs = [] if os.name == "nt" else ["-lm"]100    if subprocess.run([cc, *flags, *includes, str(c_path), "-o", str(exe), *libs]).returncode != 0:101        sys.exit(1)102 103 104def load_started() -> dict:105    try:106        return json.loads(STARTED.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))107    except (OSError, ValueError):108        return {}109 110 111def save_started(started: dict) -> None:112    STARTED.write_text(json.dumps(started, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")113 114 115def log_rows() -> list[list[str]]:116    if not LOG.exists():117        return []118    rows = []119    for line in LOG.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():120        cells = [c.strip() for c in line.strip().strip("|").split("|")]121        if len(cells) == 4 and re.match(r"\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d", cells[0]):122            rows.append(cells)123    return rows124 125 126def minutes(seconds: float) -> str:127    s = int(round(seconds))128    return f"{s // 60}:{s % 60:02d}"129 130 131def seconds(text: str) -> int:132    m, s = text.split(":")133    return int(m) * 60 + int(s)134 135 136def due(passes: list[dt.date]) -> dt.date | None:137    if not passes:138        return None139    return max(passes) + dt.timedelta(days=INTERVALS[min(len(passes), len(INTERVALS)) - 1])140 141 142def status() -> int:143    rows = log_rows()144    today = dt.date.today()145    started = load_started()146    print(f"{'block':<16}{'reps':>5}  {'best time, level':<18}{'last':<12}next")147    for b in blocks():148        mine = [r for r in rows if r[1] == name_of(b)]149        passes = [dt.date.fromisoformat(r[0]) for r in mine]150        best = min(mine, key=lambda r: (-int(r[2]), seconds(r[3])), default=None)151        best_text = f"{best[3]}, level {best[2]}" if best else "-"152        next_day = due(passes)153        next_text = "now" if next_day is None or next_day <= today else next_day.isoformat()154        if name_of(b) in started:155            next_text = f"started, level {started[name_of(b)]['level']}"156        last = max(passes).isoformat() if passes else "-"157        print(f"{b.name:<16}{len(mine):>5}  {best_text:<18}{last:<12}{next_text}")158    print()159    print("start one with: python tools/dojo.py start <block> <level 1 to 3>")160    return 0161 162 163def start(word: str, level: str, force: bool) -> int:164    b = find(word)165    source = b / f"level{level}.rin"166    if not source.exists():167        sys.exit(f"dojo: {name_of(b)} has no level {level}; the levels are "168                 + ", ".join(p.stem[len("level"):] for p in sorted(b.glob("level*.rin"))))169    kata = b / "kata.rin"170    untouched = [p.read_text(encoding="utf-8") for p in b.glob("level*.rin")]171    if kata.exists() and kata.read_text(encoding="utf-8") not in untouched and not force:172        sys.exit(f"dojo: {kata.relative_to(ROOT)} has your work in it; add --force to replace it")173    shutil.copyfile(source, kata)174    started = load_started()175    started[name_of(b)] = {"level": int(level), "at": dt.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")}176    save_started(started)177    target = targets(b).get(int(level))178    print(f"{kata.relative_to(ROOT)} is level {level}" + (f"; the target is {target}" if target else ""))179    print(f"the clock is running. Test it with: python tools/dojo.py {name_of(b)}")180    return 0181 182 183# Run a program, printing what it prints as it prints it, and keep the text to184# look for PASS in.185def stream(cmd: list[str]) -> tuple[int, str]:186    lines = []187    with subprocess.Popen(cmd, cwd=ROOT, text=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT) as p:188        for line in p.stdout:189            print(line, end="", flush=True)190            lines.append(line)191    return p.returncode, "".join(lines)192 193 194def check(word: str, args: list[str]) -> int:195    b = find(word)196    if not (b / "kata.rin").exists():197        sys.exit(f"dojo: no kata.rin in {b.relative_to(ROOT)} yet; start one with: "198                 f"python tools/dojo.py start {name_of(b)} 1")199    passthrough = [a for a in args if a != "--sanitize"]200    exe = OUT / name_of(b) / ("harness.exe" if os.name == "nt" else "harness")201    build(b / "kata.rin", exe, "--sanitize" in args)202    code, out = stream([str(exe), *passthrough])203    if code != 0 and not any(line.startswith("FAIL") for line in out.splitlines()):204        traced = subprocess.run([str(exe), *passthrough, "--trace", "1"], cwd=ROOT, text=True,205                                stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)206        ops = [l for l in traced.stdout.splitlines() if l.startswith("operation ")]207        print("the harness crashed" + (f"; the last operation it started was\n    {ops[-1]}" if ops208                                       else " in the scenario, after the last step printed above"))209    if code != 0 or "PASS" not in out.splitlines():210        return 1211    started = load_started()212    entry = started.pop(name_of(b), None)213    if entry and not passthrough:214        took = (dt.datetime.now() - dt.datetime.fromisoformat(entry["at"])).total_seconds()215        if not LOG.exists():216            LOG.write_text("# Dojo log\n\n| date | block | level | time |\n|---|---|---|---|\n", encoding="utf-8")217        with LOG.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:218            f.write(f"| {dt.date.today().isoformat()} | {name_of(b)} | {entry['level']} | {minutes(took)} |\n")219        save_started(started)220        target = targets(b).get(entry["level"])221        print(f"\nlevel {entry['level']} in {minutes(took)}" + (f", target {target}" if target else ""))222        passes = [dt.date.fromisoformat(r[0]) for r in log_rows() if r[1] == name_of(b)]223        print(f"logged in {LOG.relative_to(ROOT)}; {name_of(b)} is due again on {due(passes).isoformat()}")224    return 0225 226 227def play(word: str) -> int:228    b = find(word)229    exe = OUT / name_of(b) / ("playground.exe" if os.name == "nt" else "playground")230    build(b / f"play_{name_of(b)}.rin", exe, False)231    return subprocess.run([str(exe)], cwd=ROOT).returncode232 233 234def main() -> int:235    args = sys.argv[1:]236    if not args:237        return status()238    if args[0] in ("-h", "--help", "help"):239        print(__doc__)240        return 0241    if args[0] == "start":242        rest = [a for a in args[1:] if a != "--force"]243        if len(rest) != 2:244            sys.exit("dojo: start <block> <level>")245        return start(rest[0], rest[1], "--force" in args)246    if args[0] == "play":247        if len(args) != 2:248            sys.exit("dojo: play <block>")249        return play(args[1])250    return check(args[0], args[1:])251 252 253if __name__ == "__main__":254    sys.exit(main())

dojo/dojo.rin

1// What every harness in the dojo shares: the run's settings, a random number2// generator that gives the same numbers everywhere, how a step is checked, and3// how a failure is reported. It also holds the two types the katas take as4// given: a handle, and a status.5//6// The harnesses import it, and so does every kata file that uses a handle or7// a status:8//9//   import "../dojo.rin"10 11import "std/print.rin"12import "std/memops.rin"13import "std/vec.rin"14import "std/fmt.rin"15 16// A generational handle: an index, and which life of that index it was made17// for. Generations start at 1, so a zeroed handle, `{}`, is never alive and can18// mean "no handle".19dojo_handle: struct = {20    index: u32;21    generation: u32;22}23 24// What a change reports. `dead` means the handle no longer names anything25// alive, so nothing changed.26dojo_status: enum[must_use] = {27    ok,28    dead,29}30 31dojo_handle_eq: proc(a: dojo_handle, b: dojo_handle) -> b32 = {32    return a.index == b.index && a.generation == b.generation;33}34 35// Writes `index:generation`.36dojo_fmt_handle: proc(f: *fmt, h: dojo_handle) -> void = {37    fmt_u64(f, cast(h.index, u64));38    fmt_char(f, ':');39    fmt_u64(f, cast(h.generation, u64));40}41 42dojo_status_name: proc(s: dojo_status) -> ^const char = {43    return s == dojo_status.ok ? "ok" : "dead";44}45 46dojo_bool_name: proc(b: b32) -> ^const char = {47    return b ? "true" : "false";48}49 50// One harness run: which block, the fuzz seed, how many operations, where to51// stop for the debugger, and whether to print each operation. The command line52// sets them:53//54//   harness --seed 42 --ops 5000 --stop 1337 --trace 155dojo_run: struct = {56    block: ^const char;57    seed: u64;58    ops: u64;59    stop: u64;60    trace: u64;61}62 63dojo_parse_u64: proc(text: ^const c8, out: *u64) -> b32 = {64    value: u64 = 0;65    i: u64 = 0;66    while (text[i] >= '0' && text[i] <= '9') {67        value = value * 10 + cast(text[i] - '0', u64);68        i += 1;69    }70    out* = value;71    return i > 0 && text[i] == 0;72}73 74dojo_run_init: proc(argc: i32, argv: ^^c8, block: ^const char, title: ^const char) -> dojo_run = {75    run: dojo_run = {};76    run.block = block;77    run.seed = 1;78    run.ops = 20000;79    for (i: i32 = 1; i < argc; i += 2) {80        value: u64 = 0;81        if (i + 1 >= argc || !dojo_parse_u64(argv[i + 1], value&)) {82            printfmt("usage: harness [--seed N] [--ops N] [--stop N] [--trace 1]\n");83            exit(2);84        }85        if (strcmp(argv[i], "--seed") == 0) {86            run.seed = value;87        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], "--ops") == 0) {88            run.ops = value;89        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], "--stop") == 0) {90            run.stop = value;91        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], "--trace") == 0) {92            run.trace = value;93        } else {94            printfmt("usage: harness [--seed N] [--ops N] [--stop N] [--trace 1]\n");95            exit(2);96        }97    }98    printfmt("dojo: {}\n", title);99    return run;100}101 102// A step of the scenario: what was done, what came back, and what should have.103// Printed when it matches; the end of the run when it does not.104dojo_same: proc(what: ^const char, got: ^const char, want: ^const char) -> void = {105    if (strcmp(got, want) != 0) {106        printfmt("FAIL in the scenario: {} gave {}, it should give {}\n", what, got, want);107        exit(1);108    }109    printfmt("    {}: {}\n", what, got);110}111 112dojo_fuzz: proc(run: *dojo_run) -> void = {113    printfmt("fuzz: {} operations from seed {}, checked after each\n", run*.ops, run*.seed);114}115 116// Set a breakpoint here, and run with --stop N.117dojo_stopped_at: u64 = 0;118 119dojo_stop_here: proc(op: u64) -> void = {120    dojo_stopped_at = op;121}122 123// Call before operation `op`. It returns 1 when the operation should be124// described, and the caller prints the description and a newline: with125// --trace, every operation is, so a crash shows the last one that started;126// with --stop at this operation, it is, after dojo_stop_here has run, so a127// breakpoint there lands just before it.128dojo_before: proc(run: *dojo_run, op: u64) -> b32 = {129    if (run*.stop == op) {130        dojo_stop_here(op);131        printfmt("stopped before operation {}: ", op);132        return 1;133    }134    if (run*.trace != 0) {135        printfmt("operation {}: ", op);136        return 1;137    }138    return 0;139}140 141// A failure in the fuzz run, in three parts: dojo_fail starts the line, the142// caller prints what went wrong and a newline, and dojo_failed says how to get143// back here in the debugger and ends the run.144dojo_fail: proc(run: *dojo_run, op: u64) -> void = {145    printfmt("FAIL at operation {} (seed {}): ", op, run*.seed);146}147 148dojo_failed: proc(run: *dojo_run, op: u64) -> void = {149    printfmt("    debug it: build/dojo/{}/harness --seed {} --stop {}\n", run*.block, run*.seed, op);150    printfmt("    with a breakpoint on dojo_stop_here, which runs just before that operation\n");151    exit(1);152}153 154dojo_pass: proc() -> void = {155    printfmt("PASS\n");156}157 158// splitmix64: a few lines, fast, and the same numbers on every machine and in159// rust-dod's dojo, so a seed means the same run everywhere. u64 arithmetic160// wraps, as splitmix64 wants.161dojo_rng: struct = {162    state: u64;163}164 165dojo_rng_next: proc(r: *dojo_rng) -> u64 = {166    r*.state = r*.state + 11400714819323198485'u64;167    z: u64 = r*.state;168    z = (z ^ (z shr 30)) * 13787848793156543929'u64;169    z = (z ^ (z shr 27)) * 10723151780598845931'u64;170    return z ^ (z shr 31);171}172 173// A number in 0..n.174dojo_rng_below: proc(r: *dojo_rng, n: u64) -> u64 = {175    return dojo_rng_next(r) % n;176}

"ecs/src/3.systems/3.1.queries/queries.rin",29    "ecs/src/3.systems/3.2.systems/systems.rin",30    "ecs/src/3.systems/3.3.commands/commands.rin",31    "ecs/src/3.systems/3.4.game/game.rin",32 33    // Advanced: layout and SIMD, docs/README.md34    "src/1.aos_vs_soa/aos_vs_soa.rin",35    "src/2.archetype_table/archetype_table.rin",36    "src/3.many_archetypes/many_archetypes.rin",37 dojo/README.md43    "dojo/1.free_list/play_free_list.rin",44    "dojo/2.swap_remove/play_swap_remove.rin",45    "dojo/3.slot_map/play_slot_map.rin",46    "dojo/4.column/play_column.rin",47
